themes.name: Home as Place vs. Home as People
themes.description: The knight is defined by a fixed place and a fixed loyalty; the Emberkin are defined by never being allowed to stay. The love story is these two definitions of belonging colliding.
themes.resolution: Unresolved by design -- the tragic choice forces him to pick one definition of home and forfeit the other.

themes.name: Oaths Make and Unmake Belonging
themes.description: His oath binds him to a home; the Emberkin's ancient broken oath damns them to none. A man who lives by his word falls for a people cursed for breaking theirs.
themes.resolution: The book weighs whether an oath is worth more than the life it costs to keep.

themes.name: Duty Chosen vs. Duty Imposed
themes.description: The knight's duty is freely sworn; the Emberkin's is a curse laid upon them. The story sets a chosen chain beside an inherited one and asks whether either can be laid down.
themes.resolution: Tragic -- neither binding proves escapable without irrevocable loss.

themes.name: The Stories Kingdoms Tell About the Expelled
themes.description: The knight is sent believing the Emberkin are a threat; captivity teaches him the gap between the crown's justification and the people themselves. Prejudice as the polite face of expulsion.
themes.resolution: His changed understanding cannot change the machinery already in motion.

themes.name: Loving What You Cannot Keep
themes.description: A cursed, wandering people can never offer a home; honest gold funds only the next leg of an endless road. To love one of them is to love the road with no end.
themes.resolution: The romance's power is its impossibility; the ending is sacrifice.
